question: When a dismissed cron job recovers while no Control UI tab is observing it and later fails again, when should the failed-cron chip reappear?
rationale: Source inspection cannot choose the intended UX tradeoff between durable snoozing and reliably surfacing later incidents; job-id-only identity hides unseen recurrences, while run identity can re-nag on every scheduled failure.

options.title: Bound the snooze
options.body: Expire failed-cron dismissals after a defined interval so accepted incidents stay quiet temporarily but later unseen failures eventually resurface.

options.title: Key every failed run
options.body: Include a stable run or incident identity so each later failed execution resurfaces, accepting that persistently failing recurring jobs may nag again every schedule tick.

options.title: Require observed recovery
options.body: Keep job-id-only signatures and explicitly accept that recoveries not observed by an open tab cannot re-arm later failures.

recommendation.title: Bound the snooze
recommendation.body: Expire failed-cron dismissals after a defined interval so accepted incidents stay quiet temporarily but later unseen failures eventually resurface.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a Control UI snooze and attention-policy decision, with cron ownership input needed for incident identity.
